note:
ISO 2026-W48 runs from November 23 through November 29. Venus is about 0.6° in ecliptic longitude from Spica in Virgo. To find Mars, first identify Leo, trace the Sickle, and locate Regulus in that pattern. Mars lies about 1.0° away in ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot; use the finder to transfer from Regulus to the planet.

**Naked eye:** 🌕 Full Moon · Moon Before Yule — 14:53:34 UTC. Bright moonlight favors prominent stars and planets while reducing contrast on faint deep-sky objects. Use Cih, β Phe, Mirach as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -12.3; direct motion; 96.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude Nov 24 14:53 UTC. Conjunction with Ceres in ecliptic longitude Nov 28 01:12 UTC. Conjunction with Uranus in ecliptic longitude Nov 24 17:06 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -0.6; direct motion; 67.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -4.9; direct motion; 20.8% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 0.6; direct motion; 89.6% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; retrograde motion; 97.7% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Nov 28 01:12 UTC. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.1; direct motion; 99.1% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.6; retrograde motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.6; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude Nov 25 22:41 UTC. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Nov 24 17:06 UTC. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace Sculptor’s charted figure in the finder, then identify α Scl at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** PacMan Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 300: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 362: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; IC 1613: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Phi Cassiopeiae Cluster: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: Astronomical lunar phase near opposition to the Sun.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.

story_candidates.dek: Cih is a star in Cas; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 0h 56m and declination +60.7°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star is circumpolar (at 45° declination it touches the geometric horizon at lower culmination). It reaches approximately 74° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Cas constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
